chunks: Al-Husayn from Fadalah from Hammad ibn 'Uthman from 'Amir ibn Nufaym al-Qummi said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'The houses that people occupy, in which there is the urine of animals and dung, and in which enter the Jews and Christians, how is prayer to be performed in them?' He said, 'Pray on your garment.'
ai.seo_question: How should one perform prayer in a house that contains animal urine or is entered by non-Muslims?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) addresses the practical concern of praying in mixed-use dwellings (*manazil*) that may contain impurities like animal urine or be frequented by non-Muslims. He prescribes praying on one's own garment (*thawb*) as a sufficient precautionary measure to ensure the validity of the prayer, reflecting the Shia principle of ease (*taysir*) in ritual purity when absolute certainty of cleanliness is difficult to maintain.
